Specifies which classes of statements will be logged by session audit logging. Multiple classes can be provided using a comma-separated list and classes can be subtracted by prefacing the class with a - sign.

Specifies that session logging should be enabled in the case where all relations in a statement are in pg_catalog.  Disabling this setting will reduce noise in the log from tools like psql and PgAdmin that query the catalog heavily.
Specifies whether audit messages should be visible to the client. This setting should generally be left disabled but may be useful for debugging or other purposes.

Specifies the log level that will be used for log entries. This setting is used for regression testing and may also be useful to end users for testing or other purposes.  It is not intended to be used in a production environment as it may leak which statements are being logged to the user.
Specifies that audit logging should include the parameters that were passed with the statement. When parameters are present they will be be included in CSV format after the statement text.

Specifies whether session audit logging should create a separate log entry for each relation referenced in a SELECT or DML statement. This is a useful shortcut for exhaustive logging without using object audit logging.
Specifies whether logging will include the rows retrieved or affected by a statement.
Specifies whether logging will include the statement text and parameters.  Depending on requirements, the full statement text might not be required in the audit log.

Specifies whether logging will include the statement text and parameters with the first log entry for a statement/substatement combination or with every entry.  Enabling this setting will result in less verbose logging but may make it more difficult to determine the statement that generated a log entry, though the statement/substatement pair along with the process id should suffice to identify the statement text logged with a previous entry.

Specifies the master role to use for object audit logging.  Multiple audit roles can be defined by granting them to the master role. This allows multiple groups to be in charge of different aspects of audit logging.

Push supported scalar array operations down to DocDB for evaluation.

Enables update of reltuples in pg_class for the base table and index after creating the index. When disabled, reltuples are not updated during concurrent index creation and only index reltuples are updated during non-concurrent index creation.
Sets the boolean flag to enable or disable upsert mode for writes.
If set, all fields that vary from run to run are hidden from the output of EXPLAIN
Batch size of explicit row locking
Set to true when upgrading extensions during a YSQL major version upgrade.

[This is an advanced flag, avoid using it unless recommened by Yugabytesupport.] If object locking is enabled, concurrent DDLs are allowed. This is done by using the new mode for catalog reads and writes using PG's catalog snapshot. Set this flag to true for falling back to the legacy mode which involves using pggate's catalog read time for catalog reads when running a DML transaction (and) the transaction snapshot for catalog reads and writes when running a DDL transaction. Concurrent DDLs will not be supported if this flag is set. If object locking is disabled, only the legacy mode is used.
Enable fast-path transaction for copy on colocated tables. For testint now.
Maximum number of rows to fetch per scan. 0 = No limit
Maximum size of a fetch response. 0 = No limit
Sets the maximum size for the FK reference cache filled by the INSERT, SELECT ... FOR KEY SHARE or similar statmements
Sets the staleness (in ms) to be used for performing follower reads.

Controls whether ysql follower reads that is enabled inside a transaction block should take effect in the same transaction or not. Prior to fixing #20482 the behavior was that the change does not affect the current transaction but only affects subsequent transactions. The flag is intended to be used if there is a customer who relies on the old behavior.

Make the next DDL update the catalog in force mode which allows it to operate even during ysql major catalog upgrades. WARNING: This is a dangerous option and should be used only for DDLs on temp tables, and other transient objects.
Forces use of tablespace-based locality over region locality.
Tablespace used for tablespace-based locality. Picked automatically if InvalidOid (default).
Include DocDB metadata (such as tablet splits) in formatting functions exporting system catalog information.
Node UIDS to prefer in cost comparisons.
Ignore boolean condition for row count estimate in legacy cost model.
Ignore the FREEZE flag on COPY FROM command.
Ignores requests to set pg_class OIDs in yb_binary_restore mode
When set, walsender will fetch the publication as of current time if it encounters any failures while reading the catalog tables as of yb_read_time
Ignores requests to set relfilenode IDs in yb_binary_restore mode
Delay in milliseconds between stages of online index build.
Maximum batch size for arbiter index reads during INSERT ON CONFLICT.
Invalidation messages expiration time in catalog table pg_yb_invalidation_messages.
Identifies that connection is created by Ysql Connection Manager.
Use single RPC to select and lock when PK is specified.
Sets the maximum number of transactions for which to return rows in pg_locks.
Sets the minimum transaction age for results from pg_locks.
Sets the maximum number of rows per transaction per tablet to return in pg_locks.
When a process exits, log a peak heap snapshot showing the approximate memory usage of each malloc call stack if its peak RSS is greater than or equal to this threshold in KB. Set to -1 to disable.
The compatibility level to use during a YSQL Major version upgrade. Allowed values are 0 and 11.
When set, the next ddl statement will not cause running transactions to abort. This only affects the next ddl statement and resets automatically.

Max number of invalidation messages supported for incremental catalog cache refresh.
Max number of internal query layer retries of a statement
Sets the maximum number of streams tolerated for scalar array operation merge.
Enables expression pushdown for queries in mixed mode of a YSQL Major version upgrade.
Enable pushdown of scalar array operation expressions in mixed mode of a YSQL Major version upgrade. For example, IN, ANY, ALL.
Comma separated list of additional sys cache ids that are allowed to be negatively cached.
Sets the planner's estimate of the fixed cost of fetching a batch of rows from a YB relation
Enables the use of regular transactions for operating on system catalog tables in case a DDL transaction has not been started.
The number of rows to plan per parallel worker
Approximate size of parallel range for DocDB relation scans

The drivers use message protocol to communicate with PG. The driver does not inform PG in advance about a Batch execution. We need to identify a batch because in that case the single-shard optimization should be disabled. Postgres drivers pipeline messages and we exploit this to peek the message following 'Execute' to detect a batch. This may lead to some unforeseen bugs, so this GUC provides a way to disable the single-shard optimization completely or go back to the behavior before #16446 was fixed.
Enables pg_locks to integrate and display advisory locks details correctly.
Log each request received by the YSQL webserver
Log each request received by the YSQL webserver
The interval at which Google TCMalloc should sample allocations in the YSQL webserver. If this is 0, sampling is disabled.
If enabled, choose custom plan over generic plan  for prepared statements based on the number of partition pruned.
Disable prefetching in a PLPGSQL FOR loop over a query.
If enabled, planner will force a preference of batched nested loop join plans over classic nested loop join plans.
If true, IS NOT NULL is pushed down.
If true, strict inequality filters are pushed down.
Time (in milliseconds) for which the query diagnostic's background worker sleeps
Size of query diagnostics circular buffer that stores statuses of bundles
This disables creating extra bgworker which creates database connection for query diagnostics. If this is set to true, ASH and schema details are not dumped
Control read-after-commit-visibility guarantee.
Allow any statement that generates a read request to go to any node.
Allows querying the database as of a point in time in the past. Takes a unix timestamp in microseconds. Zero means reading data as of current time.
Refresh materialized views in place.
Maximum number of changes kept in memory per transaction in reorder buffer, which is used in streaming changes via logical replication. After that, changes are spooled to disk.

Which sampling algorithm to use for YSQL. full_table_scan - scan the whole table and pick random rows, block_based_sampling - sample the table for a set of blocks, then scan selected blocks to form a final rows sample.
Silence the advisory locks error message.
Enables the comparison of old and new values of columns specified in the SET clause of YSQL UPDATE queries to skip redundant secondary index updates and redundant constraint checks.

If enabled, procedural language statements may be speculatively executed when it is safe to do so without waiting for the successful completion of previous statements. This allows any writes produced by triggers to be batched alongside their parent data-modifying writes such that the number of storages flushes may be minimized.
TCMalloc sample interval in bytes, i.e. approximately how many bytes between sampling allocation call stacks
Block the given index creation phase.
When set, inject code to make psql output stable across linux and mac.
When > 0, add a delay after applying invalidation messages.
When set, the next DDL will be delayed by this many ms prior to commit.
When > 0, add a delay before calling YBCPgSetTserverCatalogMessageList.
When set, all drops will fail
Fails index backfill at given stage.
When set, the next DDL will fail right before commit.
When set, the next increment catalog version will fail right before it's done. This only works when catalog version is stored in pg_yb_catalog_version.
When set, DDLs that rewrite tables/indexes will fail after the new table is created.
Used to test yb_index_check()
When set, fill padding bytes with zeros when creating a shared invalidation message.

When set, all DDL statements will cause the catalog version to increment. This mainly affects CREATE commands such as CREATE TABLE, CREATE VIEW, and CREATE SEQUENCE. This also enables negative catcache entries.
The number of times to force custom plan generation for prepared statements before considering a generic plan.
When set, force a full catalog cache refresh before executing the next top level statement.
Restricts the number of retries for transaction conflicts. For testing purposes.
Slows down yb_index_check() by sleeping for 1s after processing every row. Used in tests to simulate long running yb_index_check().

When set, this PG backend will stay in global catalog version mode. Used in testing to simulate a lagging PG backend during the finalization phase of cluster upgrade to a new release that has the per-database catalog version mode on by default.
Relaxes some internal sanity checks for system catalogs to allow creating them.
When set, DDLs that rewrite tables/indexes will not drop the old relfilenode/DocDB table.
The multiplier to disable_cost to add when costing ybgin index scans that may not be supported.
Size threshold in bytes for a catcache tuple to be compressed.

[DEPRECATED - instead use the yb_get_current_transaction_priority() function]. Gets the transaction priority used by the current active distributed transaction in the session. If no distributed transaction is active, return 0
Sets lower bound for priority used by transactions of this session
Sets upper bound for priority used by transactions of this session
Maximum size in bytes of columns whose data is to be compared while seeking to optimize updates. If set to 0, no size limit is applied.
Maximum number of columns whose data is to be compared while seeking to optimize updates. If set to 0, all applicable columns in the table will be compared.
Enables optimizations of YSQL UPDATE queries. This includes (but not limited to) skipping redundant secondary index updates and redundant constraint checks.
Indicates the state of YSQL major upgrade to PostgreSQL version 15. Do not modify this manually.
Enables hash splitting as the default method for primary key and index sorting in LSM indexes
[Internal Only GUC] - Help a backend identify that this is a connection from the internal Auto-Analyze service
If set, the client connection will be authenticated via 'yb-tserver-key' auth

If object locking is off (i.e., enable_object_locking_for_table_locks=false), concurrent DDLs might face a conflict error on the catalog version increment at the end after doing all the work. Setting this flag enables a fail-fast strategy by locking the catalog version at the start of DDLs, causing conflict errors to occur before useful work is done. This flag is only applicable without object locking. If object locking is enabled, it ensures that concurrent DDLs block on each other for serialization. Also, this flag is valid only if ysql_enable_db_catalog_version_mode and yb_enable_invalidation_messages are enabled.
Timeout in milliseconds to wait for backends to reach desired catalog versions.
Time in milliseconds for which Walsender waits before fetching the next batch of changes from the CDC service in case the last received response was empty.
Time in milliseconds for which Walsender waits before fetching the next batch of changes from the CDC service in case the last received response was non-empty.
If enabled, additional procedural language constructs are whitelisted for use in speculative execution.

Used to identify DDLs executed in Automatic xCluster mode target universe. For example, DDL operations will skip the data loading phase, including table rewrites and nonconcurrent indexes. Sequence restarts via TRUNCATE TABLE are also skipped.WARNING: Incorrect usage will result in data loss.
Controls the consistency level of xCluster replicated databases.
Internal use only: Used by HandleTargetDDLEnd function.
Internal use only: Used by HandleTargetDDLEnd function.
Temporarily disable automatic xCluster DDL replication - DDLs will have to be manually executed on the target.
Test override for replication role.
Shows the count of database objects that require a sticky connection within this session.
Maximum number of in-flight operations allowed from YSQL to tablet servers
Sets the maximum batch size for writes that YSQL can buffer before flushing to tablet servers.

Enter a special mode designed specifically for YSQL cluster upgrades. Allows creating new system tables with given relation and type OID. Do NOT use this unless you know exactly what you're doing, consequences may be dire!
Continues processing past damaged page headers.
